props.gloss_en: and its substitute [made] after its redemption dies

the substitute of a firstborn and of a tithe, they and their offspring and their offspring's offspring to the end of the world, are like the firstborn and tithe, and are eaten in their blemish by the owners
Abaye: each bears its mother's name; this one is wholly called the substitute of a firstborn/tithe -- as a firstborn and tithe are eaten in their blemish by the owners, so is their substitute

Abaye: and this one bears its mother's name and is called the substitute of consecrated animals -- as those are eaten only through redemption, so their substitute; and this one is not strong enough for its redemption to take hold
the baraita: whence that the substitute of disqualified consecrated animals dies? the verse says 'of those that chew the cud ... it is impure'
the stam: that [the five sin offerings that die] comes from 'of those that have a split hoof ... impure'
the baraita: whence the five sin offerings that die? the verse says 'of those that have a split hoof ... impure'
the stam: the five sin offerings that die are a received tradition
the stam (first answer, abandoned): rather, the verse came for the substitute of a guilt offering
the stam: the substitute of a guilt offering is also a tradition -- whatever in a sin offering dies, in a guilt offering grazes
the stam: from the verse alone I would say [they go] to grazing; the tradition teaches us [they go] to death
the stam: from the tradition alone I would say one who happened to eat of these five sin offerings [violates] a prohibition but no lav; [the verse] teaches us there is a lav
